prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout A/B Test Results (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Metric" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Control" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Variant" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Lift" spans 1 col × 2 row; "p-value" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 100px · one-line width 263px
  col 2: header "Control › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 52px
  col 3: header "Control › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 113px
  col 4: header "Variant › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 50px
  col 5: header "Variant › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 110px
  col 6: header "Lift" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 7: header "p-value" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 55px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare checkout outcomes for the control and variant, including uncertainty, relative lift and statistical significance.","reading":"Readers scan each metric across its row, comparing the two means and confidence intervals before checking lift and p-value. Longer metric labels can use multiple lines; the two-tier header already occupies extra height.","groups":["Control Mean and 95% CI belong together as the estimate and its uncertainty; Variant Mean and 95% CI play the same roles and should have comparable widths.","Lift and p-value are compact summaries of the comparison for each metric.","Metric labels identify the row and anchor the comparisons across it."],"keep_intact":["Individual means, percentages, currency amounts, p-values and lift values.","Time values and numeric identifiers such as 1,000.","Confidence intervals where space permits, especially the time and currency intervals."],"may_wrap":["Metric labels at word boundaries.","Confidence intervals at natural break points if needed, keeping each endpoint intact.","The p-value header if its column is too narrow."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[161,73,134,71,131,73,76],"idea":"Preserve every numeric value and confidence interval on one line, using a narrow metric column that wraps longer labels."},{"name":"B","widths":[220,71,105,70,105,73,75],"idea":"Give metric labels more room while treating the two confidence interval columns equally and allowing their longest ranges to wrap."},{"name":"C","widths":[250,71,90,70,90,73,75],"idea":"Prioritize readable metric labels and compact paired comparison columns, accepting more wrapping in confidence intervals."}]}
